A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GMValuator work. Inspection of all pages establishes that the text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original CIFAR-10 visualization and statistical valuation results in Figure 2 and Table 1, plus CelebA/StyleGAN2 qualitative matching results in Figure 3.

after.justification: v4 retains the original CIFAR-10 results in Figure 2 and Table 1 and the CelebA/StyleGAN2 matching results, now displayed in Figures 3 and 4.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same product-quantization similarity matching, top-k selection, exponential distance weighting and aggregation over generated samples. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: The CIFAR-10 training-versus-held-out comparisons and CelebA face-matching evaluation are unchanged. Both versions also list MNIST without separately displaying its experimental results. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version reports comparisons against competing data-valuation algorithms; LOO, Shapley and Banzhaf methods remain background discussion. BigGAN, StyleGAN2 and classifier-free guidance diffusion retain the same experimental roles.

E3.justification: Both retain the same nonoverlapping CIFAR-10 subsets, training on Xv1, VGG-16 embeddings with t-SNE visualization, valuation comparison against Xv2, and CelebA/StyleGAN2 evaluation. No reported evaluation setting or procedure changes.

E4.justification: The RA1–RA3 analyses remain the same: distribution visualization, training-versus-held-out valuation comparison, and high-/low-value face examples. Splitting v2 Figure 3 into v4 Figures 3 and 4 adds no new case study or analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same hypotheses, t-statistics, p-values and 0.01 significance level in Table 1, alongside unchanged threshold discussion in Section 5.3. Neither adds run counts, seeds, error bars or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values match, including Xv1/Xv2 means of 1.632352/0.319654 for BigGAN and 0.369565/0.030434 for diffusion. The t-SNE plot, face examples and reported qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The IID assumption, generative-model background, Wasserstein formulation and valuation definitions in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No formal result, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same novelty and scope claims: a first model-agnostic, training-free, post-hoc valuation approach for generative models based on similarity matching.

C2.justification: Sections 5.3 and 6 retain the same interpretations linking similarity to contribution and the same proposed privacy, content-pricing and intellectual-property applications. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The same matching details, VGG-16 embedding choice, dataset descriptions and generator choices are documented. No new hyperparameter, hardware, training-budget, code-access or data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 30 references and the same related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Citation-range compression and bibliographic formatting do not change the cited works.

P1.justification: Prose and section order remain essentially unchanged. Limited edits include changing the author spelling from Wenglong Deng to Wenlong Deng, removing the keywords line, and updating punctuation and figure references.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from one column to two, changing typography and placement of figures, tables and Algorithm 1. Table 1 changes from side-by-side model columns to vertically stacked blocks, while Figure 3(a,b) becomes separate Figures 3 and 4 containing the same images.

improvement.justification: The extensive layout revision preserves readable access to the same method, evidence and claims. Existing issues also persist, including Section 5.3 stating that the p-value is greater than 0.05 despite Table 1 reporting extremely small p-values. The presentation changes and limited editorial edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
